pin.note: Field-tuned. Pins, the headline's second clause, the primary action, focus ring, selection.

live.note: Reserved. The one live destination row, its LIVE pill, and the raised plus inside the supplied wordmark vector (which holds its green on both grounds).

live-ink.note: Paper-safe counterpart. Defined and correct, but currently drawn on no surface: the typographic wordmark plus it served was retired when the real vector shipped.

pending.note: Pending state only. Paper counterpart is pending-ink.

paper.note: The specimen panel ground. Fixed; does not invert.

paper-ink.note: Type on paper, the dark button ground on paper, and --qr-ink.

paper-soft.note: Captions, labels and secondary sentences on paper.

field.note: The page ground, and the text colour of light-on-dark buttons.

field-raised.note: One tonal step above the field. Available for a raised ink surface.

field-ink.note: Headlines on the field and the high-contrast button ground.

field-soft.note: Ledes and first-level recession on ink.

field-muted.note: Row notes, timestamps, footnotes — the second recession step.

field-rule.note: Hairlines on ink. Row dividers draw it at 55% opacity.

background.note: Incumbent :root layer. Inverts to oklch(0.18 0.005 226) under prefers-color-scheme: dark. Used by status, auth and account pages.

foreground.note: Incumbent. Inverts to oklch(0.98 0.002 226) in dark.

border.note: Incumbent hairline. Inverts to oklch(0.32 0.005 226) in dark.

dsp-yellow.note: The Paused status page's accent bar.

dsp-red.note: The Blocked status page's accent bar.

dsp-blue.note: The Not-available status page's accent bar.

dsp-green.note: Tokenised but not currently used on any shipped surface.

display.purpose: The hero headline only. Sarlotte, hand-broken, second clause in pin cyan.

headline.purpose: One per section band, capped at 20-26ch. The closing band runs a wider variant at clamp(2.4rem, 5.4vw, 4rem)/0.98/-0.02em.

title.purpose: State names and button faces. Buttons are set in Sarlotte. The wordmark is NOT a type role — it is a supplied vector asset.

figure.purpose: Measured numbers set in Sarlotte with tabular numerals: module counts, the price anchor.

lede.purpose: The sentence under a headline and the leading term of a definition row. Max 42-46ch.

body.purpose: Running copy at 52-58ch with text-wrap: pretty. Secondary copy drops to 14px and field-muted.

mono.purpose: Every destination and every code URL. A destination is always monospace.

label.purpose: Column heads, specimen captions, LIVE pill, timestamps, the contract strip. Tracking 0.12em-0.22em.

shadows.name: pin-contact
shadows.purpose: The four specimen pins only. Makes a pin a physical object sitting on paper; it is not an elevation step and must not be reused to lift a panel.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's only authored easing. Exponential ease-out for lp-rise and for button press transforms.

motion.name: lp-rise
motion.value: animation: lp-rise 620ms var(--ease-out) both; @keyframes lp-rise { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(10px); } }
motion.purpose: The single page entrance. Wrapped in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so under reduced motion rows simply exist. Initial log rows stagger at 55ms; a newly pointed row animates alone.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active state on buttons. 0.99 on the full-width action. There is no hover transform anywhere.

motion.name: border-shift
motion.purpose: Input focus and quiet-button hover. The only colour transition in the system.

motion.name: qr-module
motion.purpose: Incumbent loading mark: four QR squares light clockwise. CSS-only so it runs before hydration. Replaced by qr-breathe (opacity-only cross-fade) under reduced motion.

layers.name: incumbent

layers.behaviour: Follows the system colour scheme. Unchanged by this build.

layers.name: landing

wordmark.sizing: Width only; height computed as round(width * 320 / 778) so the ratio cannot drift.

narrative.northStar: The Specimen Sheet and the Ledger
narrative.overview:
QRiate+ ships two materials and nothing between them. On the left is paper: a near-white specimen panel carrying one real QR symbol, tacked down with four cyan pins, captioned the way a type foundry captions a cut. On the right is ink: a near-black field carrying hairline-ruled ledger rows of destinations, dates in small caps, monospace URLs, one of them live in green. The seam between the two is hard and vertical, and the argument of the whole product lives in it — the paper never changes, the ledger always does.

The system is flat, ruled and measured. Depth comes from material and tone, not from shadow or glass. There are no cards: a three-card feature row was built and deliberately removed, and its job is done instead by ruled definition lists whose hairlines carry the structure. Figures are real — the module counts, the character counts and the symbols themselves are generated by the same library that produces downloadable artwork — so the type sets them in tabular numerals at display size and lets them stand as evidence rather than decoration.

This is an extension of an incumbent system, not a replacement. The De Sign Plus oklch tokens, --radius, Sarlotte and Raleway were already here and are unchanged; the status pages and the account/auth pages still use them and still follow prefers-color-scheme. The landing layer (.lp) is new, scoped to one surface, and deliberately fixed against the colour scheme: inverting a paper panel meeting an ink field would not darken the page, it would destroy the composition.
keyCharacteristics: Two materials, one hard seam; paper for the specimen and the scan side, ink for the owner's side
Ruled, not boxed — hairlines and definition lists instead of cards
Colour as denotation: green means live, cyan means pinned, amber means pending, coral means struck
Real artefacts only: the QR symbols on screen are genuinely encoded and scan
One authored motion, from an already-visible default
Sarlotte for every heading, Raleway for every sentence, monospace for every destination

rules.name: The One Live Row Rule
rules.body: Green denotes exactly one thing: the destination that is currently live, its LIVE pill, and the raised plus in the wordmark. If green appears twice in one list, the list is lying.

rules.name: The Two-Tunings Rule
rules.body: Every accent ships twice. On the ink field use the base token; on paper use the -ink counterpart. Never put a field-tuned accent on paper — it goes faint and stops reading as a signal.

rules.name: The Fixed Material Rule
rules.body: The .lp layer does not respond to prefers-color-scheme. The paper/ink contrast is the composition, not a theme of it. Only the incumbent :root layer inverts.

rules.name: The Split-Fill Rule
rules.body: A brand asset that has to sit on both materials ships as two files, derived by fill class: near-neutral fills (chroma < 25) are re-stated for the new ground, chromatic fills are preserved untouched. Never by filter, invert() or a blend mode — those move the accents too, and the wordmark's cyan, green, amber and coral are the same four denotative colours the rest of the page depends on. Inverting them would make the mark disagree with its own system.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Sarlotte sets headings, numerals and button faces. Raleway sets every sentence. Nothing is set in a third face except a destination, which is monospace. No system display face substitutes for Sarlotte.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader could compare down a column carries .lp-num (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums, letter-spacing: 0.01em). Module counts, character counts, prices, dates.

rules.name: The Measured Column Rule
rules.body: Every text block declares a ch maximum — roughly 40–46ch for ledes, 52–58ch for body. No paragraph runs the width of the field.

rules.name: The Material Follows the Subject Rule
rules.body: A band takes paper when its subject is the scan side or the printed specimen; it takes ink when its subject is the code's owner. The page alternates by meaning, never for visual relief, and it closes on ink so it arrives somewhere.

rules.name: The Flat Field Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and flat on hover. If something needs to separate from its neighbour, rule it or change its material. No box-shadow is a legitimate way to build a container here.

dos: Do scope every new landing-family token and class under .lp, and leave the :root / prefers-color-scheme layer alone — status, auth and account pages depend on it inverting.
Do use the -ink accent variants on paper and the base accents on the ink field.
Do reserve green for the single live destination, its LIVE pill, and the wordmark's raised plus.
Do build containers from hairlines and material changes: ruled rows, definition lists, ruled figure captions.
Do set every comparable number with .lp-num and every destination in monospace.
Do keep each text block under a declared ch maximum (40–46ch for ledes, 52–58ch for body).
Do animate from an already-visible default, and wrap any new animation in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) as lp-rise does.
Do render QR symbols from the real generator at error-correction Q with their 4-module quiet zone, using --qr-ground / --qr-ink so they inherit their material.

Do place the wordmark as one of the two supplied vectors — the dark file on light grounds, the light file on the ink field — sized by width only, with PRODUCT_NAME from src/lib/brand.ts as its alt text.

Do keep PRODUCT_NAME the authority for every plain-text form of the name: titles, metadata, email, alt text, anywhere a glyph has to survive being copied or read aloud. It is no longer the source of the mark itself.
Do derive a second-ground brand asset by splitting its fills — neutrals re-stated, chromatics preserved — and shipping it as its own file.
donts: Don't put a card on the landing surface. A three-card feature row was built here and removed; rows and ruled lists do that job.
Don't add a box-shadow to build a container, a hover lift, or a resting elevation. The only shadow in the system is the 3px pin contact.
Don't use gradients, glass, blur panels (outside the mobile header's scroll scrim) or decorative tints.
Don't make the .lp layer respond to prefers-color-scheme.
Don't produce a light-ground brand asset with filter: invert(), brightness() or a blend mode, and don't re-set the wordmark as type. Both destroy the mark's accents.
Don't let an accent appear outside its denotation: amber only on pending, coral only on struck/blocked and form errors, cyan only on what can be moved.
Don't draw a fake or decorative QR symbol anywhere. Every symbol shown is genuinely encoded and scans.
Don't give the specimen symbol a key, a transform, or any render path reachable from the interaction. Its immobility is the product claim.
Don't set body copy in Sarlotte or headings in Raleway, and don't substitute a system display face for Sarlotte.
Don't invent prices, client names, logos, testimonials or counts to fill a layout. If a figure is undecided it renders as an em dash or as a sentence saying so.
